title: Migrate the controller off LVGL (spike renderer)
description: Replace LVGL with spike, a purpose-built minimal RGB565 renderer, to free ~120 KB of the cm33 256 KB flash. LVGL fixed ~150 KB overhead is the ceiling: at ~15% of the controller scope the flash is already 78% full. Companion arch-design: docs/workflow/arch-designs/spike_arch-design.md. Phases: 0 spike validation, 1 draw layer + font, 2 panel port, 3 backends + input, 4 remove LVGL.

title: Phase 3: measure cycles/voice/sample
description: DWT cycle counting on the M85: render cost per voice/sample, validate the 24-voice budget (24 voices / 4 parts / 3 reserved).

title: Refactor cm85 I2S loop into audio::Output
description: Mirror audio_out_miniaudio.cc: move the cm85 main.cc I2S loop into audio/audio_out_ssie.cc behind the audio::Output interface. Only if the interface earns its keep.

title: Reduce audio render-ahead latency
description: The render loop runs ~3 blocks ahead of the DMA (4-slab pipeline), ~5 ms note-on latency. Shrinking the pipeline is a latency-vs-underrun tradeoff.

title: Phase-0 hardware gates
description: Four bring-up gates on the board: (1) audio passthrough, (2) 440 Hz sine, (3) MIDI/RTT, (4) M33 note-on to M85 frequency. Plus verify 3.072 MHz PWM MCLK + 48 vs 44.1 kHz, the IRQ choices (29/60), SDRAM-init ordering, and remove the cm85 smoke note (M33 sole producer).

title: Move scope/fft buffers to SDRAM
description: The Ui scope ring (64K) + cycle buf (16K) + fft re/im/mag (80K) = ~160 KB is heap-allocated in SRAM (RAM at 71%). Design study Option C: place them in SDRAM (0x68000000).
close_reason: Ui/scope/fft moved to SDRAM in b9d9ee5

title: MIDI input transport
description: Gate #3. Decide the transport (USB host for the X-Touch vs UART DIN), then wire MIDI input on the cm33. Blocked on the transport decision.

title: Velocity sensitivity
description: Replace the kVoiceGain=0.25 stopgap with per-note velocity. Engine + params changes; desktop-testable.

title: Initial prototype
description: Remaining work to reach a working initial prototype on the EK-RA8D2: control-surface completion (touch, MIDI), engine features (velocity), memory cleanup (scope/fft to SDRAM), and hardware bring-up (Phase-0 gates, Phase-3 measurement).

title: Wire FT5336 touch on iic1
description: Capacitive touch (focaltech,ft5336 at 0x38) for the 7-inch 1024x600 panel on iic1 + the parallel-graphics connector; feeds LVGL pointer input. Reference: boards/shields/rtklcdpar1s00001be.overlay (swapped-x-y). Board-gated.

title: Bake Zephyr Python build deps into the Dockerfile
description:
## Context

The Zephyr target build needs Python packages absent from the Docker image.
They were installed ad-hoc into the container's system site-packages with
`pip3 install -r zephyr/scripts/requirements-base.txt`, which is wiped on every
image rebuild. The SDK, Zephyr tree, and `west` are already baked or live in
the persistent /workspace — the Python deps are the one thing that is not.

## Problem

On a fresh container, `west build` fails at CMake configure with
"Missing jsonschema dependency" (zephyr_module.cmake:73). The deps must be
re-installed by hand after every restart.

## Fix

Bake the Zephyr base build requirements into the Dockerfile pip layer
(alongside `west`). Install the packages from
`zephyr/scripts/requirements-base.txt` that the build actually imports
(jsonschema, PyYAML, pyelftools, pykwalify, packaging, intelhex, semver,
anytree, …), skipping the test/compliance extras
(requirements-build-test.txt / requirements-compliance.txt) that are not needed
to build.

## Expected

A fresh container runs `west build -b ek_ra8d2/r7ka8d2kflcac/cm85 …` with no
`pip3 install` step — the deps are present in the image.

## Evidence

First build failed at configure: `CMake Error … Missing jsonschema dependency`
(zephyr_module.cmake:73). `requirements-base.txt` is the "required to build"
set; `requirements.txt` pulls the test/compliance extras that are unnecessary.
close_reason: Baked the Zephyr build-imported Python deps (jsonschema, pykwalify, PyYAML, pyelftools, packaging, intelhex, anytree, semver) into the Dockerfile pip layer. Verification (fresh-image west build) pending image rebuild.

title: Cut control-rate powf/tanf coefficient recompute (dirtiness tracking)
description:
## Context

`bench --breakdown` (5 s, desktop) shows the full voice at ~9.9 ns/sample, of
which "env+coeff+overhead" is 5.28 ns (53%) — more than the SVF filter itself
(2.65 ns). Oscillator 1.96 ns; filter/osc ratio 1.35x.

## Problem

`update_filter_coeffs()` (engine/engine.cpp) runs unconditionally every
control step (16 samples). It maps normalized cutoff -> Hz via `powf` and
computes the TPT SVF `g` via `tanf`, even when nothing changed (fixed cutoff,
sustain, filter_env=0). This violates the digest's own "dirtiness tracking"
principle: coefficients are recomputed that did not need recomputing.

## Fix

1. Replace the exponential cutoff->Hz mapping (`powf`) with a lookup table or
   cheap polynomial — control-rate accuracy does not need `powf`.
2. Add a dirtiness flag: recompute SVF coefficients only when the effective
   cutoff/resonance changes (parameter setters, or envelope crossing a
   threshold), not every control step.

## Expected

Full voice ~10 -> ~7 ns/sample on desktop. Proportionally larger win on the
M85, where `powf`/`tanf` are software-emulated (no FPU).

## Evidence

`bench --breakdown`: osc 1.96, filter 2.65, env+coeff+ovh 5.28, full 9.90 ns/sample.
close_reason: Dirtiness tracking in UpdateFilterCoeffs: skip the pow/tan recompute when env_cutoff+Q are unchanged; sentinel in StartNote. Bench -38% coeff, -23% full voice.
